findings.description: Rejecting a proposed replacement permanently prevents agents from proposing another replacement for the original decision.
findings.failure_mode: An agent supersedes decided row A, setting A.supersede_proposed_by to B. Rejecting B updates only B, leaving A's pointer intact. Every subsequent agent supersede of A fails with 'a replacement is already proposed', even though B is rejected.
findings.suggested_fix: When rejecting a replacement, atomically clear the original row's supersede_proposed_by if it points to that replacement. Include both rows in verification.

findings.description: Import commits ledger rows before performing fallible reference rewrites, without recording an import identity for safe retries.
findings.failure_mode: If an existing --rewrite target is in an unwritable directory, mktemp fails after verify_and_swap has committed the imported rows. The command exits unsuccessfully and leaves the pending file. Retrying imports the same decisions again under fresh DEC IDs; references already rewritten during a partial attempt can retain the earlier IDs.
findings.suggested_fix: Prepare and validate rewrite outputs before committing, and persist the pending-to-DEC mapping or an import identity so retries resume safely without appending duplicate decisions.

findings.description: op_confirm only refuses on live_run_signal (RUNNING state, fresh marker, env vars), but then calls derive_attribution 0, which checks the broader is_unattended. is_unattended also fires on the 'prd' signal (a PRD whose **Status** line contains 'autonomous' or 'unattended'). In that state derive_attribution silently drops --answer-ref with a WARN and REF becomes empty, so the confirm jq sets .decided_by = .proposed_by (typically 'agent') instead of 'operator', while the transition says by: operator:decisions-command. decisions.md rule 3 states the cli: ref is what records decided_by: operator. The same inconsistency makes op_reject on a decided row die with 'the context is unattended' for the operator whenever the PRD status says autonomous, even with no run active.
findings.failure_mode: Operator confirms rows via /decisions while grimoires/loa/prd.md carries an autonomous/unattended Status line (a normal state for a project built in run mode). Every confirmed row is permanently recorded as decided_by: agent, misattributing the operator's decision in the audit ledger; rows are append-only so this cannot be corrected without supersede. Operator reject of a decided row is refused outright in the same state.
findings.suggested_fix: In op_confirm (and the operator branches of op_reject/op_supersede) gate on live_run_signal only, and make derive_attribution skip the unattended override when is_operator_call && ! live_run_signal. Alternatively exclude the 'prd' signal from is_unattended for operator-recorded calls. Add a bats case: PRD Status autonomous + confirm --answer-ref cli:... must yield decided_by: operator.

findings.description: import copies every row of the pending file into the live ledger after only a schema validation (validate-artifact.sh --type decisions) and PEND-id rewriting. It never checks row status, decided_by, decided_by_ref or transitions. A pending file is agent-authored (the header says 'written outside the main checkout') and can trivially contain status: decided, decided_by: operator, or status: superseded rows. verify_and_swap treats all imported ids as 'touched', so its invariants do not catch this. This bypasses the stated invariant that 'a row becomes decided only' through /decisions confirm, which is the core trust property of the ledger.
findings.failure_mode: An agent (or a run in a linked worktree) writes or edits decisions-pending.yaml with status: decided and decided_by: operator rows, then the lead runs the documented `import --from` step. The live ledger now contains operator-attributed decided rows the operator never confirmed; grimoire-index and `list --not-decided-by operator` hide them from the review surfaces.
findings.suggested_fix: Before allocating ids, reject the import unless every pending row has status in {open, proposed, rejected}, decided_by == null, and (decided_by_ref == null or not matching OPREF_RE unless the import is an operator call); also require transitions[*].by to not start with 'operator:'. Optionally force status to proposed on import so confirmation always goes through /decisions.

findings.cross_file_justification: decisions.md and user-invoked-commands.txt claim disable-model-invocation makes confirm/reject-decided/context --clear operator-only; the only runtime enforcement in dec-write-lib.sh is a string compare on --recorded-by.
findings.description: The operator-only guard is `[[ "$(o recorded-by)" == decisions-command ]]`. disable-model-invocation only stops the Skill tool from launching /decisions; the model can still run `dec-write-lib.sh confirm --recorded-by decisions-command ...` through Bash, and the Karpathy/autonomous-agent docs now actively steer agents toward dec-write-lib.sh. The bats grep over command/skill bodies does not constrain runtime behaviour. The design text ('an agent that could run them would confirm its own decisions') therefore overstates the guarantee.
findings.failure_mode: An unattended or prompt-injected agent self-confirms its proposed rows by passing the magic --recorded-by value; the ledger shows decided_by: operator if it also passes a cli: ref. Only a live run signal blocks this, and that signal is absent for ad-hoc interactive sessions.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a runtime signal the model cannot forge from Bash: e.g. require an interactive TTY check plus an env token exported only by the /decisions command surface, or a PreToolUse hook that denies Bash invocations of `dec-write-lib.sh (confirm|context --clear|reject.*decided)` unless the /decisions command is the active skill. At minimum, document the guard as advisory in decisions.md and the lib header.

findings.description: A non-operator supersede records supersede_proposed_by on the decided row and refuses any further supersede while that field is set. But op_reject never clears supersede_proposed_by on the old row when the proposed replacement is rejected, and op_confirm only consumes it on confirm. After one rejected replacement, the decided row is permanently locked against agent-proposed supersedes ('a replacement is already proposed'), and the dangling pointer references a rejected row.
findings.failure_mode: Agent proposes DEC-0010 superseding DEC-0003; operator rejects DEC-0010. Any later `supersede --id DEC-0003` from a skill exits 1 forever, forcing operators to do the supersede themselves or leaving the stale pointer in the ledger.
findings.suggested_fix: In op_reject, when the rejected row has .supersedes set, also update the referenced row's supersede_proposed_by to null (add it to the touched list and keep added=0). Alternatively, in op_supersede treat a supersede_proposed_by that points at a non-proposed row as clear.
